feedFacts: StoryAngle: Mariano Rosales gets five years and $88 million. The ninth inning stays with the A's closer

Notes: Mariano Rosales came to Oakland in C39 as the young arm in the trade that sent five-time All-Star closer Edmundo Pena to Baltimore, a 26-year-old with A potential and an 89 overall, and the question then was whether he was ready to replace a legend. In C83 he was named the closer on a one-year, $10.1 million deal with free agency waiting at the end of it. That free agency is off the table now. Rosales has signed a five-year contract at $17.6 million a year, $88 million in all, running 2042 through 2046 with no contract option, and he would not reach free agency until 2047. He earned the raise in the season the A's went 127-35 and won the seventh World Series. Rosales went 8-3 with 42 saves and a 1.84 ERA in 63.2 innings, struck out 82 and walked 14, finished with 1.7 WAR and made the All-Star team, one of seven A's selected in C99. The one mark on the year came in World Series game 2, when he and Clark Saryan each gave up 2 runs in relief of Travis Coles. He goes into the new deal at 27, with a 95 overall that is still climbing, a 96 mph four-seam fastball, a 94 mph two-seamer and an 84 mph changeup. The Utah-born right-hander, a second round pick in 2035, lives in Jack London. The deal also answers part of the bullpen question this page raised in C114, whether the A's would spend on a high-end arm or turn the late innings over to rookies Saryan and Julio Valencia. The ninth inning stays with Rosales.
